#+TITLE: <Short report title — what the work was, in 4–8 words>
#+DATE: [<YYYY-MM-DD>]
#+FILETAGS: :report:<topic>:<slice|wiki|design|fix|...>:

# Agent post-action report template.
#
# Canonized 2026-05-04. Owned by @atoz (alias =@curator=) under the agent-report
# primer namespace (see docs/wiki/agent-orientation.org).
#
# How to use:
# 1. Copy this file to docs/notes/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.org
# 2. Fill every section. Delete sections that genuinely don't apply
#    (e.g. Verification when the work didn't ship code) — but DO
#    NOT delete Objective or Dev-tracking; those are load-bearing.
# 3. Keep the Objective summary tight (1–3 sentences). State what
#    was done AND why. If the work has multiple actions, name them.
# 4. Dev-tracking links use [[id:UUID][label]] form for wiki/roadmap
#    pages, and relative paths for sister notes.
# 5. Run scripts/link_wiki_files.py if your report cross-links into
#    docs/wiki/.
#
# Reference exemplars:
# - docs/notes/2026-05-04-promotions-slice-report.org (code slice)
# - docs/notes/2026-05-04-promotions-wiki-report.org (wiki draft)

* Objective

*Summary.* <1–3 sentences. What was done and why. Name the
discrete actions if there were more than one. A reader returning
to this note in three months should know from this paragraph
alone what the work was for and what it produced.>

* Dev-tracking

# Links to where this work fits in the broader project. Include:
# - The wiki concept page(s) this work realizes or extends
# - The dev-tracker phase entry (with § section reference)
# - The roadmap phase if applicable
# - Sister notes from parallel agents working on the same arc

- Wiki concept: [[id:<UUID>][<page name>]] — <one-line context>.
- Dev-tracker: [[id:9096622a-689c-4bb1-8e32-1654bce48d1c][dev-tracker.org]] § Phase <NN>
  (<phase title>). <one-line context>.
- Roadmap: [[id:43e1b335-656b-45ba-8d6d-7d9b9f2e9c4d][roadmap.org]] §
  "Phase <NN> — <title>" (<status>).
- Sister note: =docs/notes/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.org= — <relationship>.

* What landed

# Concrete artifacts. File paths + LOC deltas where useful. Tables
# work well for multi-file changes; bullet lists for one or two.
# Be specific — vague "added some code" is not useful in three months.

- =<path/to/file>= — <what changed, +/-LOC, position relative to
  surrounding code>.
- =<path/to/file>= — <new file? modification? what shape?>.

* Decisions

# Key choices made during the work. For each: what was chosen,
# what the alternatives were, why this one won. Skip purely
# mechanical decisions (variable naming, import order); keep
# load-bearing ones (schema shape, integration point, error
# handling stance).

** <Decision title>

<What was chosen, what was rejected, why. Reference the brief or
the relevant wiki rule if applicable.>

* Verification

# Only include if the work shipped runnable code OR a verifiable
# artifact (e.g. a wiki page passing link_wiki_files.py). For
# pure-design / pure-doc work where there's nothing to verify
# beyond "the file was written," delete this section.

** <Check name>

$ <command>
<output>
#+end_src

<Brief comment if the output needs interpretation.>

* Open questions

# Things the work surfaced that need a human call. Number them so
# they're easy to reference in follow-up conversation. Be specific
# about what answer would unblock what.

1. *<question title>.* <Context, why it matters, what would
   unblock it.>
2. *<question title>.* <…>

* Non-goals

# Boundaries deliberately observed. The "Hard NO" list from the
# brief, or the natural boundaries you respected even when
# tempting to expand scope. This is the section that proves you
# didn't drift; a future reviewer should be able to audit it.

- <thing not done>.
- <thing not done>.

* Gotchas

# Things a future reader (you, a sister agent, a contributor)
# might trip over. Include:
# - Surprising behaviors discovered during the work
# - Idioms in the code that aren't self-evident
# - Local-environment quirks that affected verification
# - Caveats that aren't bugs but feel like one

- <surprising thing>. <why it's not a bug, what to know>.
- <surprising thing>. <why it's not a bug, what to know>.
